subject: Catalyst Health trial — environment decision, success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Catalyst Health trial — proposed envs, success criteria, owners

Hi Elena — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposal so we have a single place to track actions.

Call summary (10m):
- Goal: 2-week POC to validate Redwood inference for chart summarization (+ privacy checks)
- Primary success criteria: end-to-end latency under 300ms median for 1k-token prompt; F1 >= 0.82 on our labeled summarization set; no PII leakage in sample audits.
- Data flow constraint: no customer PHI persisted in hosted logs; full audit logs required for dedicated/VPC.

Environment options we discussed:
1) Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted API — minimal setup, 24–48h access, limited to redaction-at-source and tech controls. Good for rapid signal but requires sample data obfuscation.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPUs in our Dedicated pool — predictable throughput, can run with customer-supplied model quantization. Requires procurement/PO for reserved capacity (lead time ~7–10 days).
3) VPC deployment (preferred by Catalyst for compliance): Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed network and KMS — strongest controls, longer setup (2–3 weeks) and an SOW.

Our recommendation for Catalyst: start on Hosted for the 2-week exploratory phase to validate model integration and prompts, then migrate to Dedicated or VPC for the compliance-focused evaluation depending on your security signoff.

Proposed success criteria (detailed):
- Latency: median <= 300ms, P95 <= 800ms, for 95th percentile of 200 concurrent sessions.
- Quality: F1 >= 0.82 on the labeled set; human review pass-rate >= 90% on a 100-sample blind set.
- Security: no raw PHI stored; pass initial data handling checklist and one sample audit.

Action owners & timeline:
- Elena (Catalyst): share an anonymized sample of 150 records + a short prioritized prompt list by Fri 8/20.
- Priyom (Redwood): provision hosted API keys, QA prompts, and sample eval harness by Mon 8/19.
- Ben (Redwood Solutions): provide Dedicated/VPC SOW options, high-level cost estimate, and provisioning timeline by Wed 8/21.
- Marissa (CS): coordinate weekly check-ins and the final eval call end of week 2.

Attachments: trial proposal (catalyst-trial-proposal-v1.pdf), standard SOW template (sow-template.docx).

Next steps: Elena to confirm sample delivery timeline; I will send Hosted API access and the eval harness once we receive the sample. If you prefer to skip Hosted and go straight to VPC, flag that in your reply and Ben will send a tailored SOW.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — this is very clear. A couple of clarifying Qs before we commit to Hosted:
1) For the hosted path, can you confirm whether full request/response logs (even masked) will ever be accessible out of region (we need EU data residency for some records)?
2) Can you confirm whether the hosted eval will support our token limits (we have prompts up to 1,500 tokens)?

We can deliver an anonymized 150-record set by Fri 8/20 as requested; prefer to keep initial run on Hosted assuming logs can be restricted and masked. If not, we'll ask for Dedicated or VPC options.

—Elena

Hi Elena — quick notes on the infra side addressing your questions:
- EU residency: Hosted API can be scoped to EU region endpoints; logs are stored in the selected region but note processing occurs on multi-region infrastructure for failover. For strict EU-only residency we recommend Dedicated in an EU region or VPC.
- Token limits: Hosted supports up to 2,048-token prompts in current model versions; we can batch and stream larger contexts if needed.
- Cost/timeline: Hosted access — same-day to 48h once we receive the sample. Dedicated provisioning for a short reserved pool: ~7–10 business days (depends on PO). VPC setup: 10–18 business days including network provisioning and KMS onboarding.

If you want, I can prepare a short comparison table and a one-page SOW for the three paths. Ben

--
